title: Grammar — 100 Sentences: Parts of Speech & Sentence Types

cards.front:
[A] little boy walked beside the large dog.
What kind of word is highlighted?
A. Subject Noun (SN)
B. Verb
C. Article
D. Adjective
cards.back:
C. Article
Why? “A” is an article because it is one of the three articles: a, an, and the. “A” introduces one nonspecific person, animal, place, or thing.

D. Object of Preposition
cards.back:
D. Object of Preposition
Why? The object of a preposition is the noun or pronoun that completes the preposition’s meaning. Find the preposition “around.” Ask “Around what?” The answer is “garden,” so “garden” is its object.

cards.front:
The young fox rested [beneath] the tree.
Which kind of word shows a relationship such as where?
A. Adverb
B. Article
C. Preposition
D. Adjective
cards.back:
C. Preposition
Why? A preposition shows a relationship, such as where something is, when it happens, or which direction it goes. “beneath” begins the phrase “beneath the tree” and connects the action to a place or thing. That makes it a preposition.

cards.front:
A cheerful child sang [softly] at home.
Which kind of word answers HOW an action happens?
A. Adjective
B. Adverb
C. Article
D. Preposition
cards.back:
B. Adverb
Why? An adverb gives more information about a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. Many adverbs answer “How?”, “When?”, or “Where?” Ask “How did the action happen?” “softly” tells how the action was done, so it is an adverb.

cards.front:
The [sleepy] owl watched the moon.
Which kind of word answers WHAT KIND or HOW MANY?
A. Subject Noun (SN)
B. Article
C. Adjective
D. Verb
cards.back:
C. Adjective
Why? An adjective describes a noun and can answer “What kind?”, “Which one?”, or “How many?” Ask “What kind?” about the owl. “sleepy” gives that information, so it is an adjective.

cards.front:
[An] excited puppy wagged its tail.
Which kind of word is A, AN, or THE?
A. Article
B. Subject Noun (SN)
C. Adjective
D. Verb
cards.back:
A. Article
Why? “An” is an article because it is one of the three articles: a, an, and the. “An” introduces one nonspecific thing and is used before a vowel sound.

cards.front:
The strong swimmer [dived] into the pool.
Which kind of word tells WHAT SOMEONE DOES?
A. Adjective
B. Subject Noun (SN)
C. Article
D. Verb
cards.back:
D. Verb
Why? A verb tells what someone or something does or what state it is in. Ask “What did the swimmer do?” The answer is “dived.” It names the action, so it is the verb.

cards.front:
A busy [bee] buzzed near the flowers.
Which kind of word answers WHO or WHAT does the action?
A. Article
B. Adjective
C. Verb
D. Subject Noun (SN)
cards.back:
D. Subject Noun (SN)
Why? The subject noun names who or what the sentence is about. The action verb is “buzzed.” Ask “What buzzed?” The answer is “bee.” That is the noun doing the action, so it is the subject noun.
